Goodbye 10-Step Routines, Here Are the Only Skincare Steps You Need
Daily, Weekly and Monthly 
 A simple calendar for your face: what to do every
day, what to save for the weekend and what to check once a
month.  Skincare has
a way of multiplying. One serum becomes three, a cleanser becomes a
double cleanse, and suddenly a routine that was meant to make life
easier takes fifteen minutes every night. Dermatologists have a
simpler answer: most steps do not need to happen every
day. 
 The trick is to sort your routine
by frequency. A few essentials belong in every morning and evening,
a handful of treatments work best once or twice a week, and a
couple of checks only need to happen monthly. Here is how to
organize it. 
 Every Day: The Non-Negotiables 
 Cleanse twice a day. The American
Academy of Dermatology recommends washing your face 
when you wake up, before bed and after sweating, using lukewarm
water, a mild cleanser and your fingertips rather than a rough
cloth or scrub. 
 Moisturize after cleansing,
morning and night, choosing a texture that suits your skin type: a
lighter lotion for oily skin, a richer cream for dry or mature
skin. 
 Wear sunscreen every morning. The
AAD advises a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher every
day before going outside, including in fall and winter, since UV
exposure continues year-round and is a major driver of skin
aging. 
 If you use a targeted treatment,
such as a retinoid or a vitamin C serum, keep it simple and
consistent. Many people start retinoids a few nights a week and
build up as their skin adjusts. 
 Every Week: The Boosters 
 Exfoliation is the step most
people overdo. Dermatologists interviewed by Prevention generally
recommend exfoliating between one and three times a week: once or
twice for dry, sensitive or mature skin, two or three times for
oily or acne-prone skin. Board-certified dermatologist Dr. Toral
Vaidya advises adjusting “the frequency based on how your skin
looks and feels.” 
 Gentle chemical exfoliants, such
as lactic or mandelic acid, are often easier on the skin than
gritty scrubs. If your skin stings, looks red or feels tight, cut
back. 
 A hydrating or soothing mask once
a week is optional but pleasant, especially as indoor heating dries
the air. This is also the right moment to wash your makeup brushes
and sponges and to change your pillowcase, which helps keep
bacteria and oil away from your face. 
 Every Month: The Checks 
 Examine your skin. The Skin
Cancer Foundation recommends checking your skin from head to toe
once a month and seeing a dermatologist at least once a year for a
full-body exam. Look for anything new, changing or unusual, and get
it checked right away. 
 Review your products. Once a
month, look at what you are actually using, toss anything expired
or that has changed smell or texture, and notice whether your skin
needs something different as the seasons change. 
 The Bottom Line 
 A good routine is not the longest
one. It is the one you can follow consistently. Cleanse, moisturize
and protect every day, exfoliate a few times a week and check in
with your 
skin once a month. Everything else is a bonus, and
your skin will likely look better for having a little less to deal
with.
